**Nuka-World On Tour** is a location in *Fallout 76*, introduced in the *Nuka-World on Tour* update. It is located southwest of Lewisburg, in the Ash Heap region of Appalachia.

Nuka-World On Tour was a traveling show founded before the Great War. Originally, its showrunners were Randall and Muriel Myers, but after their passing it was taken over by their children Pete and Pat. Only a few of the original founding members remain, including Del Walsh and Gunther Jenkins, as the rest have either gone missing or were lost fending off raiders from attacking the attraction. [1] Nuka-World On Tour is now set up near Lewisburg, as the traveling carnival was revisiting Pre-War show locations. [2] Betty Hill is the newest member of the traveling show. [3] 

Upon their arrival in Appalachia, the Overseer of Vault 76 visited the troupe in order to deliver them the vaccine for the Scorched Plague. [4] 

The Nuka-World On Tour location consists of five main areas. The center hub of the traveling circus consists of a large platform crafting station that has an Armor Workbench, Tinker's Workbench, Punch Card Machine, Power Armor Station, Chemistry station, and Cooking Station. There is also a Scrapbox, as well as an Ammo Storage Box.

Across the way from the crafting hub, there sits the Nuka-Cade, where one can find Chloe the Clown, Bruno the Strongbot, and Lady G the Fortune Teller. Pat can usually be found walking around this area between the Nuka-Cade and the crafting hub. Around the Nuka-Cade there are some mini games and booths, where one can usually find Pete sitting at a picnic table on the left. Just past Pete and behind the Nuka-Cade there is a Nuka-Cola fountain machine where the player can buy an assortment of Nuka-Cola drinks.

To the left of the Nuka-Cade is the Wild West Showdown attraction, where just outside Gunther can be found standing. The Nuka Launcher is found at the very top of the hill, and underneath it is the entry to the Tunnel of Love. The Tunnel of Love can only be entered during the event of the same name. Beside the closed doors is the stand where Betty can be found. At the bottom of the hill, below the crafting hub, is the giant tent for the Spin the Wheel attraction.

A number of Caravans for the accompanying staff, located on a hill south of the Wild West Showdown. Cluttered around the camp are an Armor Workbench, two Cooking Stations, Tinker's Workbench and a Weapons Workbench, in addition to a terminal and several notes.

- Angry Note - Note, at the staff caravans, on a table in between two red caravans.
- Betty's Journal - Note, at the staff caravans, on a small stand next to the southernmost blue caravan.
- Complaint To A Mad Man - Note, at the entrance to Wild West Showdown, on the ground next to Gunther Jenkins.
- Del's Journal - Note, at the staff caravans, on a dresser in the easternmost red caravan with the Tinker's Workbench.
- Gunther's Journal - Note, at the staff caravans, on a dresser inside the westernmost red caravan.
- Note to Pete - Note, at the staff caravans, on a dresser inside the northernmost blue caravan with the Armor Workbench.
- Pat's Journal - Note, at the staff caravans, on a nightstand inside the southernmost blue caravan with the Manager's Terminal.
- Pete's Bandit Roundup Highscores - Note
- Pete's Journal - Note, at the staff caravans, on a bed inside the northernmost blue caravan with the Armor Workbench.
- Terrible Show - Note, at the entrance to Wild West Showdown, on a Fire Barrel next to Gunther Jenkins.

Nuka-World On Tour appears in *Fallout 76*, introduced in the *Nuka-World on Tour* update.
